title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Ch. V, 'Algèbre des figures', 1986). A 'figure' F on a finite set S = |F| is encoded as a surjection f: S -> I onto an ordered index set I. The elements A of F are indexed by I, and each has an 'open star' (or open stratum) A° = A°(F). A subfigure G <= F with support T = |G| corresponds to a closed part J of I with T = f^{-1}(J). A refinement F' <= F with the same support is a factorisation S -> I' -> I, where φ: I' -> I is surjective; p.34 says h is a 'coinitial surjection'. G' is the subfigure of F' induced over T, so J' = φ^{-1}(J).

Page 32 proved that F\G and F'\G' coincide under the hypotheses considered. It then set up the equivalence of conditions b), c), d) by putting U = |F| \ |G| = |F'| \ |G'|, I* = F\G = I \ J and I'* = F'\G' = I' \ J'. These are open parts of the ordered index sets.

This page: since J' = φ^{-1}(J), φ restricts to a surjection φ* = φ|I'*: I'* -> I*. The projection p: U -> I* factors as p = φ* ∘ p', with p': U -> I'* surjective.
- The open stars of F' contained in U, i.e. those not indexed in G', are exactly the fibres of p'.
- The open stars of F contained in U are exactly the fibres of p.

The conditions then read:
- b) says φ* is bijective.
- c) says every fibre of p, i.e. each A° for A in F\G, is a fibre of p'. Since the p-fibres are unions of p'-fibres over the φ*-fibres, and φ* is surjective, this is 'evidently equivalent' to b).
- d) needs an auxiliary fact, quoted from earlier (in this context): for A in F, A ∈ F' iff A°(F) is an open star of F'. Hence d) says that for each A_i in I*, the star p^{-1}(A_i) ⊂ U is a star of F'. This again amounts to injectivity, hence bijectivity, of φ*.

Conclusion: b ⇔ c ⇔ d.

Margin warning: 'φ* bijectif ! Attention ! Mais φ* pas iso !!'. A monotone bijection of ordered sets need not be an order isomorphism. So the conditions give only a set-level identification F\G = F'\G'; whether φ* is an order isomorphism needs an extra condition, possibly involving c).

The page then starts on the equivalence with a). Here F'' is as in a), with index set I''. The diagram is S = |F| = |F'| = |F''| -> I'' -> I (composite φ), containing T = |G| = |G'| -> J' -> J. The argument breaks off there; it is continued on p.34 by recasting refinements and induced subfigures as factorisations of S -> I compatible with T -> J.

Purpose: a combinatorial theory of poset-stratified finite sets ('figures'). It characterises refinements of a figure that change nothing off a closed subfigure, i.e. that are 'concentrated over G'.
errors: Top diagram: the transcription's 'I ↪ I' = φ^{-1}(J)' should read J' ↪ I' with J' = φ^{-1}(J), above J ⊂ I, a closed part ('partie f[ermée]'). As transcribed the diagram is inconsistent.

The step 'd) ⇒ φ* bijective' relies on the criterion 'A ∈ F' iff A°(F) is an open star of F''. This is cited as already proven, but on p.32 it rests on a lemma announced 'plus bas', so the proof is not self-contained at this point.

Grothendieck himself flags a subtle point: bijectivity of φ* does not make it an order isomorphism. The equivalence b⇔c⇔d is therefore only set-theoretic. This is not an error, but it is a caveat on what the conditions mean.
The page writes 'p bijectif' in the conclusion of d). Logically it should be φ* bijective (or injective), since p itself is not bijective; this is a slip or a misreading.

ideas.what: Encoding a stratification or figure on a finite set as a surjection S -> I onto an ordered index set. Refinements are factorisations S -> I' -> I, and subfigures are preimages of closed (downward-closed) parts.
ideas.modern_name: Poset-stratified spaces / stratifications as maps to posets with the Alexandrov topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in MacPherson, Treumann; made standard by Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A), Barwick–Glasman–Haine (exodromy)
ideas.where_published: Not in published texts. The 'Algèbre des figures' chapter is unpublished; related themes appear vaguely in Récoltes et Semailles reflections only.

ideas.what: Open stars of the strata as fibres of the projection U -> I*. Comparing two stratifications via the induced map of index sets, a refinement trivial off G iff φ*: I'* -> I* is bijective.
ideas.modern_name: Refinement of stratifications; fibres of a stratification map

ideas.what: Warning that a bijective monotone map of posets need not be an isomorphism.

missed.claim: This is an early (1986) combinatorial treatment of poset-stratified sets as surjections onto ordered sets, with refinements as factorisations. It predates by decades the now-standard 'stratification = map to a poset' formalism. The page itself only contains routine lemmas.
missed.quote: les étoiles ouvertes de F' qui sont ⊂ U ... sont les fibres de U --p'--> I'*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest: it documents Grothendieck working with the exodromy-style poset formalism for stratifications, which is absent from his published texts.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine combinatorial lemma: the equivalence of conditions for a refinement to be trivial off a closed subfigure. It is correct and elementary. Historically mildly interesting as an unpublished use of the poset-stratification formalism, but there is no new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'J' ↪ I' = φ^{-1}(J)' (not 'I ↪ I''). The bottom row is 'I ⊃ J partie f[ermée]'.
The label struck/marked near the right of the top diagram reads 'surjectif' (with a struck 'surj...').
'les [A] Str.les ouvertes' is plausibly 'les strates/étoiles ouvertes'. The handwriting is ambiguous; p.32 used 'strate ouverte'.
The left margin reads roughly: 'Attention ! φ* bijectif mais pas iso !! Mais φ* iso ⟺ φ* bij. + ... (c))'. That is, a warning that a bijective monotone φ* need not be an order isomorphism.
The insertion near 'Notons que' reads roughly '(sans hypothèse, pour F' ≤ F)'.
'd) dit que pour A_i ∈ F\G = I*, l'étoile p^{-1}(A_i) ⊂ U est une étoile de F''. Here p^{-1}, not p'^{-1}.
The bottom diagram: 'S = |F| = |F'| = |F''|', 'S → I'' --φ''--> I', 'T = |G'| = |G| → J' → J'. Several diagonal strokes cross out part of it.
